chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Dawud from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid said: He narrated to us al-Hasan ibn Matil al-Daqqaq and others from the scholars, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, who said: He narrated to us al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

"Command our Shias to visit the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), for visiting it increases sustenance, prolongs life, and repels various evils, and visiting it is obligatory upon every believer who acknowledges his Imamate from God."
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and legal benefits of visiting the grave of Imam al-Husayn in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* underscores the theological weight of Ziyarat al-Husayn, framing it not merely as a devotional act but as a mandatory confirmation of divine Imamate for every believer. The narration links physical well-being—specifically increased sustenance (rizq) and longevity (umr)—to spiritual obedience, reflecting the Shia tradition that views the Ahl al-Bayt as conduits of divine blessings and protection from calamities.
